Illustrated Codex Edition
Synced with playable build v10: animated flowing water and swaying treetops; Tiyanak half-height, Aswang/Manananggal/Tikbalang hero-height, Kapre 1.75× hero-height, and Bakunawa tripled in size. Title screen, customization, fitted loot and the boss campaign remain. Click any portrait or stage painting to inspect it full-size.

v10 Adventure Refinement

The game no longer awards arcade scores. Kapre now lifts a wooden club and smashes the earth; bosses unleash stronger Earthsplitter impacts. Wearable relics repaint and reshape the heroine's fitted costume parts, and weapon relics retain the current fighting-style silhouette.

✦ Official Companion Codex ✦

Likha: Chronicles of the Spirits

An offline Filipino folklore action RPG. Explore painted locations, choose one of five fighting styles, defeat myth creatures, collect relics, and survive boss stages. This codex keeps combat controls, equipment rules, and enemy counters in one place.

Getting started: Open the game to see Start · Options · Quit. Select Start to customize your guardian, choose a weapon, and select Begin to enter the sanctuary. Use Options for graphics/audio settings. Quit attempts to close the tab. Browsers that block JavaScript tab closing instead exit the game to a blank page.

Slot 1 • Doblete

Arnis (Dual Sticks)

Damage: 15 (22 finisher)
Cooldown: 0.17s
Range: 64–76 px
Knockback / Stun: 90 / 0.08s

Fast alternating stick strikes. Every third hit lunges farther and deals 1.45× damage.

Best for building quick combos against small enemies.

Slingshot

Damage: 22 (42 charged)
Cooldown: 0.34s
Range: 480 px
Pierce / Stun: 1 (3) / 0.10–0.35s

Ranged stone shots. Hold for 0.42s to charge a piercing shot with 1.9× damage.

Use against flying enemies or targets across water.
Slot 3 • Tungkod

Staff

Damage: 26 (35 wave)
Cooldown: 0.42s
Range: 105–127 px
Knockback / Stun: 220–297 / 0.22s

Wide 135° sweeps. Every third strike releases a 360° wind shockwave.

Shield

Bash DMG: 20
Reflect DMG: 2.2× incoming
Range / CD: 66 px / 0.48s
Knockback / Stun: 340 / 0.75s

Hold to guard and reflect projectiles; tap to shield-bash. Guard consumes stamina.

Reflect ranged attacks and guard against bosses.

Damage: 38 (55 vs stunned)

Range: 76 px
Knockback / Stun: 200 / 1.15s

☾ Mythical Bestiary

Painted creatures of Likha — click any sprite to enlarge
Stage 1+ • Swarmer

Tiyanak

Base HP: 34
Speed: 150
Damage: 10

A frightening infant-like creature in Filipino folklore.

Small, fast enemy that pounces in groups. Watch for its crouch before leaping.

Counter: Staff sweeps or quick Arnis strikes.
Stage 1+ • Stalker

Aswang

Base HP: 65
Speed: 122
Damage: 16

A shape-shifting nocturnal creature in Philippine folk stories.

Fast stalker with a lunging claw combo. Interrupt the attack windup or keep your distance.

Counter: Stun with Solo Baston or shoot from range.
Stage 2+ • Ranged Flyer

Manananggal

Base HP: 55
Speed: 95
Damage: 14

A flying, separated-bodied creature from Philippine folklore.

Flying enemy that crosses terrain and fires wing bolts. Ranged weapons work best.

Counter: Tirador shots or Kalasag reflections.
Stage 3+ • Charger

Tikbalang

Base HP: 115
Speed: 105 (440 charge)
Damage: 22

A horse-headed trickster said to mislead travelers.

Telegraphs a straight charge. Dash sideways or stun it before it rushes.

Counter: Dash sideways during the charge warning.
Stage 4+ • Brute

Kapre

Base HP: 180
Speed: 68
Damage: 26 (16 ember)

A large tree-dwelling figure often portrayed smoking.

Slow, heavy giant resistant to knockback. Uses close-range slams and fiery projectiles.

Counter: Reflect embers with Kalasag; avoid the slam.
Stage 30 • Final Boss

Bakunawa

Base HP: 850 (scales/stage)
Speed: 115
Damage: 28 + Eclipse Skills

A moon-swallowing serpent in Philippine mythology.

Serpentine boss that crosses obstacles and launches tidal and lunar projectiles.

Counter: Dodge tidal warnings and reflect lunar orbs.

Wear What You Loot

Living Equipment

v10 tailoring refinement: Equipment-specific pigments now follow the actual woven, leather, leaf, moonlit, storm, or golden materials. Armor paint is trimmed to the heroine’s existing torso and skirt, reducing the extra-arm and thigh artifacts visible on older outfits. Each glove, boot, and headpiece keeps its own identity, even when wearing mixed collections.

Defeat creatures, pick up a glowing relic, open I or the 🎒 button, and select Equip. The equipped piece immediately changes the hero’s visible outfit in the game and the satchel preview. Unequip it to restore the original look.

Headwear follows the face; garments and shoulder pieces turn with the torso; gloves follow hands; footwear follows animated feet. Weapon charms attach to the current fighting style without changing its attacks.

Five Folklore Collections

Distinct Worn Styles

Balangay: woven sailcloth and salakot. Balete: bark and vines. Amihan: feather and cloud fabric. Kidlat: storm-metal accents. Mayari: moon-silk and pearls. Collected parts match by color and decorative motifs.

Stat Rolls & Trade-offs

Positive & Negative Modifiers

Relics can roll DMG, ATK SPD, SPD, CRIT, MAX HP, or STUN bonuses. Higher rarity may grant extra stats; some items also have penalties.

Bag & Salvaging

Restrictions & Salvage

Collect relic drops before they disappear. Check level and character restrictions before equipping; dismantle unwanted items for Pilak.

§ Philippine Folklore & Martial Arts Glossary

Cultural terms woven into Likha: Chronicles of the Spirits
TermMeaning & Cultural Origin
BantayTagalog for “guardian” or “watchman” — the nocturnal protector of the barangay.
LikhaA Filipino word for something created or made; the title evokes a world shaped by spirits and stories.
Doblete / Solo BastonFilipino Martial Arts (Arnis/Eskrima/Kali) styles for dual-stick and single-stick combat, traditionally crafted from rattan or dense kamagong ironwood.
KalasagTraditional carved hardwood war shield carried by pre-colonial Philippine warriors.
Tirador / TungkodTraditional wooden Y-frame slingshot (tirador) and hardwood walking or fighting staff (tungkod).
Putong / SalakotTraditional warrior cloth headband (putong) and wide woven conical hat (salakot), both appearing as Headgear relics.
Bathala / DiwataBathala is the supreme creator deity in Tagalog mythology; Diwata are benevolent nature spirits bestowing biyaya (blessings).
LahoTraditional term for a lunar eclipse, attributed in Visayan and Bicolano myth to the giant sea serpent Bakunawa swallowing the moon.
Alitaptap / KulintangAlitaptap are forest fireflies glowing across the bamboo groves; kulintang is a traditional gong-chime ensemble inspiring the ambient soundtrack.
Madali / Sakto / MahirapTagalog words for Easy, Just Right, and Difficult; the current game uses a fixed Normal adventure setting.

Living World & Myth Scale

Nature Animation · v10

Water

Painted rivers gain moving glints and downstream highlights; water pools show slow currents and expanding ripples. Banks and rocks stay fixed.

Creature Height

Normal encounters: Tiyanak ½ guardian height; Aswang, Manananggal and Tikbalang 1×; Kapre 1.75×. Bakunawa's original art height is tripled, with responsive fitting on small screens.

Forest

Tree canopies sway independently while trunks remain rooted. Existing equipment, title screen and mobile controls remain available.

Visual scaling changes monster artwork rather than combat statistics. Boss variants keep their existing extra size multiplier. Under Options, animation and atmosphere settings control living-world motion.

v10 includes flowing painted rivers, gently swaying trees, tuned myth-creature sizes, original regional orchestral music, and fitted equipment. In gameplay, select the 📖 book icon to open the built-in Codex. To browse this full Wiki, use the sidebar.

Music of the Five Lands

Each outdoor stage now features an original, calming orchestral loop. The sanctuary has its own welcoming theme. All four houses and shops share the same warm indoor melody; returning outdoors restores the area's theme automatically.

  • Kagubatan ng Kawayan — flute, harp, and leaves-in-the-wind melody
  • Barangay sa Tabing-Ilog — lilting riverside woodwind and strings
  • Lumang Sementeryo — gentle nostalgic strings and oboe
  • Tuktok ng Bundok — soaring mountain flute and warm horn
  • Lawa ng Bakunawa — peaceful moonlit harp, choir, and flute
  • Kuta ng Barangay — welcoming homecoming orchestral theme
  • Every shop and house — the shared Hearthlight indoor theme

The game attempts automatic playback. Some browsers require the first click or tap to unlock audio. Use Options → Background Music to mute or re-enable.
